subject: MSA & Order Form: SLA negotiation — uptime, credits, maintenance runbook
messages:
From: Maria Sanchez <maria.sanchez@stratalytics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratalytics.com <procurement@stratalytics.com>, Juris Team <juris@stratalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: MSA & Order Form redlines — SLA and support items attached

Grace,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Attached are Stratalytics' redlines to the MSA and the Order Form focused on SLA/support items — uptime guarantees, monthly credit formula, and what we consider "maintenance" carveouts. High level asks: 1) uptime at 99.99% for API endpoints, 2) no hard cap on monthly credits (they want a full invoice credit for severe outages), and 3) maintenance windows limited to 8 hours/month with advance notice.

We also flagged response times: P1 = 30 minutes, P2 = 4 hours. Please confirm Redwood can provide the measurement methodology (how downtime is calculated, regional vs global incidents) and the types of evidence we can expect for a credit claim.

Target: we need a consolidated redline back by your legal team by Thursday 12/23 so procurement can present internally on Friday. Happy to jump on a call Monday if that helps.

Attachments: Stratalytics_MSA_redlines_20261219.pdf; OrderForm_SLA_Table_20261219.xlsx

—Maria Sanchez
Director, Procurement
Stratalytics Inc.

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Maria Sanchez <maria.sanchez@stratalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — SLA and support items attached

Maria — thanks for sending the redlines and the clear asks. We reviewed the attachments and discussed internally with Sales and Legal (cc'd). High-level response and proposed compromises below so you have our starting position before legal consolidates redlines: 

1) Uptime target: Stratalytics requests 99.99% (p0 APIs). Our standard for this tier has historically been 99.95% with tiered credits. Proposal: commit to 99.95% with an optional "Performance SLA" appendix for 99.99% at a higher committed spend (we can map to Dedicated capacity).

2) Credit formula: We understand the need for meaningful remediation. We propose a tiered credit ladder: 99.95–99.0% = 5% credit, 99.0–95.0% = 15% credit, <95% = 25% credit, with a monthly cap at 15% of that month's invoice (we can discuss increasing to 20% in exceptional scenarios). This balances customer protection and platform stability.

3) Maintenance windows: We can agree to a standard maintenance envelope of up to 6 hours/month for planned maintenance with 72 hours' notice. Emergency maintenance for critical security patches will be reasonable and notified as soon as possible; we propose a carveout clause that exempts emergency security patches from credit triggers if they are announced and documented.

4) Response times: We can commit to P1 response within 1 hour (acknowledge + triage) and P2 within 4 hours. P1 resolution SLA will depend on severity and may require escalation to Dedicated capacity or fallback model variants.

5) Measurement & evidence: We'll define downtime based on successful request rate at the region level (api.region.redwood.com) and we'll provide an audit bundle (uptime metrics, trace IDs, and KV cache logs) within 5 business days for valid claims. Legal note: need to define what constitutes a "valid claim" and the timeline for submitting claims.

Next steps: Hannah, can Legal consolidate a single redline PDF with our proposed language and a short commentary on the evidence/timing points? Marissa, please review the credit cap proposition and paper the Dedicated appendix pricing options. Maria — Grace and I propose a 30-minute alignment call Tuesday 12/21 at 10:00 PT to walk through the tradeoffs. Does that work for you?

Attachments: SLA_summary_proposal_Grace_20261220.docx

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Sanchez <maria.sanchez@stratalytics.com>, procurement@stratalytics.com <procurement@stratalytics.com>, Juris Team <juris@stratalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — legal commentary and clarifying requests

Thanks Grace — I'll own the consolidation. A few legal-practical requests / counteritems to clarify before we send a consolidated redline: 

• Measurement granularity: we need to be explicit if uptime is measured per region or global. Measuring at per-region level reduces unintended credit exposure during regional provider incidents; recommend "region-level measurement with global aggregation for multi-region outages."

• Evidence and claim window: we will accept claims accompanied by the audit bundle described by Grace. Legal requests: evidence delivered within 5 business days, claim submitted within 30 days of incident close, and a 45-day window for Redwood to remediate or credit.

• Credit cap: commercial asks for uncapped credits in case of severe outages. Legal is uncomfortable without a contractual ceiling. Proposed legal counter: cap at 20% per invoice for sustained outages unless root cause is Redwood negligence proven by audit (exception path triggers executive review). We can offer a one-time waiver for the first 12 months with additional remedies (service credits + extended support) to show goodwill.

• Maintenance: define "planned" vs "emergency" and require Redwood to publish a rolling 90-day maintenance calendar for planned work when customer is on Dedicated or has an SLA appendix. Also, require reasonable efforts to schedule high-impact maintenance in low-traffic windows for Stratalytics' region.

• Fallback and rollbacks: add language on automatic fallback to a compatible model variant and on disruption caused by model rollouts. If an upgrade causes degradation, credits should accrue from the time degradation is detected to when rollback completes.

I'll produce a consolidated redline PDF with tracked language and a short cover memo explaining the legal positions on measurement, caps, and evidence. Target to get that to Maria by EOD 12/20 so you can review before Tuesday's call.

Attachments: legal_commentary_redlines_20261220.pdf

—Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Maria Sanchez <maria.sanchez@stratalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form redlines — meeting confirmed and action items

Maria — thanks for the fast turnaround on the matrix and for being flexible. Confirming our 30-minute alignment call today 12/21 at 10:00 PT (Google Meet link in calendar invite). Summary of agreed action items before the call: 

1) Redwood Legal (Hannah) to deliver consolidated redline PDF + cover memo (evidence, measurement, caps) — delivered 12/20 (see attached).
2) Sales (Marissa) to prepare a Dedicated appendix price note for 99.99% performance SLA and to confirm whether a spend commitment can buy higher uptime tiers — deliverable 12/22.
3) CS (Grace) to provide a draft maintenance/runbook clause and proposed emergency patch carveout language — included in the consolidated redline.

If we get alignment on the cap (legal proposes 20% with a potential one-time waiver) and the measurement method, procurement indicated they can move to internal approval cycle next week. If procurement needs a higher credit ceiling, please flag during today's call so Marissa and I can loop in VP Sales for escalation.

Related links: hubspot deal and consolidated drive folder above.

Thanks — see you on the call.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
